findings.note: Mapping-form transitions have two silent-acceptance holes in an otherwise strict validator (workflow.go:3 claims 'Every rule is static'). (a) workflow.go:425-426 does `if from == "*" { continue } // the implicit *->failed rule` BEFORE strictNode, so the whole value mapping of any `*->X` key is never validated and the target is never checked. (b) workflow.go:157 declares rawTransition.On and workflow.go:429 admits "on" on EVERY mapping-form key, but addTransition (workflow.go:452) builds the Transition from From/To/Gate/Outcome/Loop only, so `on:` outside the wildcard line is decoded and dropped. Verified empirically with a scratchpad -overlay probe test (no repo file touched): a document containing `"discover -> adjudicate": {gate: findings_nonempty, on: gate_error}`, `"*->done": {on: gate_error}` and `"*->nowhere-at-all": {on: nonsense, gate: not_a_gate}` parses with err == nil and yields exactly 3 transitions -- an undeclared target, an unknown gate and a bogus `on` value all pass silently. A user who writes `*->failedd` or believes they redirected gate errors elsewhere gets no error, while machine.go:824 hardcodes workflow.FailedState regardless. Fix: validate the `*` line's target is `failed` and its body against {on}, and restrict "on" to that line (or drop the field).

evidence.note: wildcard key skipped before strictNode; body and target never validated
rawTransition.On decoded at 157, admitted at 429, never read by addTransition at 452

findings.note: The raw (unfiltered) branch measurement at gitcontext.go:93-99 is production logic that no test verifies. Mutation-proven: with `ctx.BranchRawDiffBytes = raw` replaced by `_ = raw` via a scratchpad -overlay (repo untouched), `go test ./...` passes across the ENTIRE module. The only two mentions of BranchRawDiffBytes in any _test.go are branchfiles_test.go:321-322, which merely marshal a hand-built Context to assert the JSON shape -- they never exercise the measureBranchFiles path. TestBranchFilesExcludeGenerated (branchfiles_test.go:261-288) is the one test that reaches the `len(effectiveExcludes) > 0` branch, and it asserts only the BranchFiles paths and the filtered sum, never that raw exceeds filtered. This matters because internal/contextprofile/profile.go:87-88 uses BranchRawDiffBytes as the profile's reported rawDiffBytes, and internal/prready/review.go:700-702 overwrites git.RawDiffBytes with it. Also uncovered on the same function: the Exceptions branch at gitcontext.go:81-83 (go tool cover -func puts collectWith at 86.4%; the uncovered blocks are 75.3, 82.3 and 97.4), so CollectWithExcludesExcept's new branch-measurement path is exercised by nothing. Add an assertion that BranchRawDiffBytes > BranchFilteredDiffBytes when excludes hide content, and one collectWith case with Exceptions.

findings.note: SKILL.md:56-57 states unconditionally: 'After a fix round only the edited file's shard and the cross-shard result go ignored: re-review those two and leave the rest.' That holds only while the plan's bucket count is unchanged, and the doc omits the precondition. internal/contextprofile/shards.go:201 computes `bits := bucketBits(needBuckets(total, budget))` from the TOTAL branch-diff bytes, and shardIDForPath (shards.go:122-134) derives each path's bucket as `value >> (64 - bits)`. needBuckets is ceil(total/budget) and bucketBits rounds up to the next power of two, so a fix round that moves `total` across a power-of-two multiple of the 60,000-byte budget re-buckets EVERY path: all shard ids and all shard hashes change and every committed result is invalidated at once. This plan uses two-hex-digit ids spanning 00..3f, i.e. 6 bits / 64 buckets, which means total currently sits in (1.92 MB, 3.84 MB] -- a fix round shedding enough bytes to cross 1.92 MB drops it to 5 bits and reflows everything. An orchestrator that follows the sentence literally re-reviews two shards, re-runs, and burns an attempt from the --max-attempts budget on a wall of 'missing shard result for shard-XX' blockers. State the precondition (results survive only while plan bucketing is unchanged; compare the new plan.json's planHash/shard ids before reusing results).

evidence.note: unconditional claim that only the edited file's shard is invalidated
bucket count derives from total bytes, so shard ids are not stable across a size change that crosses a power-of-two boundary

findings.note: The sdlc-loop-cmds fixture does not carry the properties the spec that introduces it asserts. docs/specs/2026-08-27-metareview-0.9.0-fsm-cli.md:257-258 says: 'user workflow testdata/fsm/workflows/sdlc-loop-cmds.yaml (declares cmds: + on_overflow + a `cmd` convergence atom; scenarios {cmd-guardrails, overflow-handler, custom-outcome})'. Checked against the tree: the fixture's convergence is `any: [{max_iterations: 1}]` (sdlc-loop-cmds.yaml:23-24) with NO cmd atom -- test-fsm.sh:213 has to write its own fixtures/cmd.yaml to get one; and `ls testdata/fsm/scenarios/sdlc-loop-cmds/` returns only `overflow-handler`, so cmd-guardrails and custom-outcome do not exist. The same spec section's outcome map claims `custom` is asserted by a custom-outcome scenario in the 'every outcome' row, but no workflow or fixture in the repo declares `outcome: custom`, so run.OutcomeCustom (internal/fsm/run/types.go:29) and its acceptance by workflow.go:690 validOutcome are never exercised end to end. The same gap is repo-wide in that spec's §5 inventory (sdlc-loop names 10 scenarios, 2 exist: happy, injection; review-loop names 7, 2 exist: clean, reviewed). Either add the fixture's cmd convergence atom and the missing scenarios, or amend the spec inventory to the scenarios that ship.

evidence.note: convergence is `any: [{max_iterations: 1}]` -- no cmd atom, contradicting fsm-cli spec line 257
cmds/on_overflow are present, but only the overflow-handler scenario dir exists; cmd-guardrails and custom-outcome are absent

findings.note: workflow.go:44 declares `MaxTimeout = 3600 * time.Second` and nothing in the module ever reads it (grep over all *.go finds only the declaration). The bound it names is hard-coded twice as a bare literal instead, at workflow.go:301 (`*rc.Timeout < 1 || *rc.Timeout > 3600`) and in the error text at workflow.go:302. Its sibling DefaultTimeout on the line above IS used (workflow.go:292). Either use MaxTimeout in the guard or delete it -- a named constant that the check does not consult is exactly the kind of drift where a bound gets changed in one place only.

evidence.note: MaxTimeout declared but never referenced; parseCmds hard-codes 3600 instead

findings.note: fake.go:9-10 documents the fake as 'Unset answers return zero values', but RevParse is the one method that does not: for a ref absent from Refs (and not literally "HEAD") it returns an errs.E(CodeGit, "unknown ref") rather than the zero string (fake.go:44). The behaviour is the more useful one -- a test that forgets to script a ref gets a loud ERR_GIT instead of a silent empty SHA -- so the code is right and the sentence is wrong. Amend the comment to say unset answers return zero values except RevParse, which errors on an unscripted ref.

evidence.note: doc comment 'Unset answers return zero values'
RevParse returns errs.E(CodeGit, "unknown ref") for an unset ref, contradicting the comment
